item.title: Dubai news: ‘Evacuate the office?’ Standard Chartered responds to viral rumours in UAE emirate amid Iran vs US-Israel war
item.description: Amidst escalating Iran vs US-Israel war, Standard Chartered clarified reports of a Dubai office evacuation, stating it extended existing work-from-home measures as a precaution. The bank emphasised its regional operations remain active. This comes as other financial institutions also implement safety protocols, highlighting Dubai's crucial role as a financial hub facing geopolitical risks.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Why the US is sending assault ship USS Tripoli, thousands of marines to the Middle East and what it means for Iran vs Israel war
item.description: The US is significantly expanding its military presence in the Middle East, deploying thousands of Marines and the amphibious assault ship USS Tripoli amid escalating tensions with Iran. This move aims to deter further Iranian aggression, protect vital shipping lanes like the Strait of Hormuz and provide the US with greater response options in the rapidly widening regional conflict.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: France returns African talking drum: The sacred instrument that once 'spoke' to entire villages and warned of danger
item.description: A sacred Ivorian drum, the Djidji Ayokwe, has returned home after over a century seized by French colonial forces. This massive talking drum, vital for community communication and a symbol of Ebrie identity, was repatriated following a special French law. Its arrival in Abidjan marks a significant moment for cultural justice and historical remembrance.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: First photo released of man who rammed car into Michigan Jewish preschool
item.description: A naturalized US citizen from Lebanon, Ayman Ghazali, rammed his car, laden with mortar shells, into a Jewish pre-K in Michigan. Security guards intervened, stopping him from causing further harm. The attack followed the deaths of two brothers, believed to be Hezbollah terrorists, in Lebanese airstrikes.

item.title: ‘Almost love’ trap explained: What is limerence trend in modern dating that makes you think about someone 24/7?
item.description: Experts reveal that intense romantic obsession, often mistaken for love, is actually limerence. This psychological state, characterised by constant thoughts and emotional highs/lows based on perceived reciprocation, can dominate lives for years. Understanding limerence helps identify unhealthy patterns, with uncertainty and modern dating potentially fuelling its intensity, guiding individuals towards healthier connections.

Is Netanyahu dead? Internet claims recent video of Israeli PM 'AI-generated' as it shows '6 fingers', sets rumour mills running amid Iran vs US-Israel war
item.description: A video of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has ignited a social media storm. Users on X claim the footage is AI-generated, pointing to distorted hands as evidence. The viral tweets and videos highlight growing public suspicion of digital media amid geopolitical tensions and Iran vs US-Israel war. The incident underscores the challenges of discerning truth in an era of synthetic content and information warfare.

item.title: 11 Indian nationals accused of staging robberies to claim crime victim visas in US
item.description: Eleven Indian nationals face US charges for allegedly orchestrating staged armed robberies at convenience stores. The scheme aimed to allow store clerks to falsely claim victim status on immigration applications for U Visas. Several defendants were arrested across multiple states, with some appearing in federal court.

item.title: ‘Are you saying I need an extra seat?’ Woman slams airline over size comment
item.description: A frequent flyer, Erika, was allegedly told by a Southwest gate agent she needed to purchase an extra seat due to her size. Despite the airline's policy requiring additional seats for passengers encroaching on neighboring space, Erika claims she fit comfortably in one seat. She later received a refund for the incident.

item.title: Romans used human feces as medicine: 1,900-year-old vial from Turkey reveals shocking treatment
item.description: A 1,900-year-old Roman glass bottle from Turkey has yielded direct chemical proof of ancient physicians using human feces as medicine. Scientists identified human excrement mixed with thyme oil, matching descriptions by the famed physician Galen. This discovery confirms ancient medical texts and offers a rare glimpse into Roman healing practices, highlighting the surprising remedies once considered legitimate.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: ‘Putin might be helping them’: Trump hints Russia could be aiding Iran
item.description: President Trump suggested Vladimir Putin might be aiding Iran in its conflict, drawing a parallel to US support for Ukraine. This comes after Trump previously questioned a reporter on similar reports. Meanwhile, a US envoy stated Russia denied sharing intelligence with Iran, though expressed hope this remains true.

item.title: The Cheese ritual: Inside the 660-year-old Dutch market where men in white race with giant cheese wheels
item.description: Alkmaar, Netherlands, revives a centuries-old cheese trading ritual every summer Friday. Dressed in white, guild members perform a synchronized trot, transporting heavy cheese wheels. This historic market, dating back to 1365, showcases traditional hand-clap bargaining and weighing, offering a vibrant glimpse into the nation's rich dairy heritage and past commercial prowess.
